newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Former Bulgarian prime minister shot dead.
newsitem.headline: Former Bulgarian prime minister shot dead.

text.p: Former Bulgarian prime minister Andrei Lukanov, now a parliamentarian for the ruling Socialists, was found shot dead at his home, the parliamentary speaker said on Wednesday.

Blagovest Sendov told parliament at the opening of its session on Wednesday that the circumstances of Lukanov's death were still not clear. Sendov appealed to deputies to keep calm and closed the session.
Bulgarian radio said deputies rose to their feet in a mark of respect to their dead colleague.

The radio said the Parliamentary Group of the Democratic Left, of which Lukanov was a member, held a brief meeting but leader Stefan Gaytandzhiev said he had no official information on what exactly had happened.
The interior ministry and police declined to give any more details.
The area where Lukanov lived in Sofia was surrounded by police. Neighbours, who declined to be named, told Reuters he was shot twice in the head while leaving his house.

Lukanov, 58, who combined business interests with poilitics, served as a communist prime minister for six months in 1990. He resigned due to widespread public dissatisfaction with the sluggish pace of reform.
In July, he was dropped as board chairman of a Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company, Topenergy, in a move designed to improve its troubled relations with the current Bulgarian government.
